## Overview

There's a new class of AI model out from TypeSafe called Jev, their flagship model. It comes from TypeSafe AI, a San Francisco lab that came out of stealth on September 15, 2026 with $40M in seed funding and Jev as its first public model.

## What is Jev?

TypeSafe's Jev is a new class of AI model, a System One Model, that returns typed decisions with calibrated probabilities instead of text, running 40-200x faster than frontier LLMs. While Jev gives up string generation, it's optimized for structured outputs and can't hallucinate. Think of Jev as a frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out.

## SDK Support

TypeSafe provides official SDKs for Python and JavaScript alongside the raw HTTP API. There are also community SDKs available, such as an idiomatic, type-safe Elixir port of the official TypeScript AI SDK providing unified LLM integrations, streaming text and structured outputs, tool calling, and agentic workflows.

## Question Types

There are three question primitives: choice picks one option from a set, score rates against ordered levels, and noul returns a yes/no probability between 0 and 1.

## Key Features

Every question in a request is evaluated in parallel against the same state, which means batching a dozen questions into one call costs little more than asking one. State and questions share a budget of roughly 32,000 tokens — about 150,000 characters of English text — and TypeSafe reports end-to-end response times of 70–500ms, making Jev a good fit for classification, routing, extraction, scoring, and guardrail checks on the request path.

# Jev Summary

## What is Jev?

Jev is TypeSafe AI's first "System One Model" — a frontier AI designed for fast, structured decision-making within software rather than text generation. The company describes it as a "frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out."

## Key Characteristics

**Speed & Cost:** Jev achieves "end-to-end response time is 70ms-500ms" and costs "$0.042 / MTok" for input tokens with "FREE" output tokens, reportedly 40x-200x faster than comparable LLMs while being significantly cheaper.

**Type Safety:** The model guarantees no type errors and cannot hallucinate, always providing calibrated confidence scores with outputs.

## Limitations in Documentation

- Question primitives (choice/score/bool) — these aren't named or formally specified

13	ends in "?"; every node has its own `▷`. Founding evidence: this skill's own first L3

19	(2) uniform depth is a smell — subtrees legitimately differ in depth, and padding a shallow

1	# OC-PROTOCOL — filling slots, composing upward, and surfacing disagreements
2	
3	The instrument only pays off in this phase: respondents talk in streams, the tree turns the
4	stream into evidence, and the consistency machinery turns evidence into findings. Grounding:
5	the operadic-consistency result (composed-vs-collapsed agreement as a label-free quality
6	signal) applied to a human respondent — the "model" being checked is the person, and
7	disagreement is treasure, not error.
8	
9	## 1. FILL — parsing free speech into slots
10	
11	- **Quote, don't paraphrase.** Put the respondent's words in the slot; add a bracketed gloss
12	  only if needed. Their vocabulary is data (it names their true categories).
13	- **Tag inferences.** An answer placed in a slot the respondent didn't explicitly address is
14	  marked `[inferred from: …]`. Untagged inference is the protocol's cardinal sin — it
15	  manufactures agreement that will later validate itself.
16	- **Never pad.** Empty slots stay empty. A slot filled with plausible invention poisons every
17	  compose step above it.

Four things a builder should believe today
Everything else in this pool is evidence for these four. Stars, likes, and vendor multiples are not.
01
Filter, not oracle
On short text with crisp labels Jev ties or beats small LLMs. On long or fuzzy input, accuracy and confidence fall together. Confident answers (the ends) were right 90–100% of the time; the middle band is a coin flip. Put Jev in front of the model you already use.
Aman Kumar, 16k-call bench · Near Here 48/50 · Every 6/7 defects
02
Believe the quartiles, not the homepage
TypeSafe’s homepage says 193.6× faster and 444.6× cheaper versus a frontier model writing prose. Users who published their own figures report a median 7× speed-up and 30× cost cut. Latency median is real: 76 ms across 333 figures.
OpenChamber analysis of 12,759 tweets, updated 19 Sep 2026
03
Decompose, then recombine in code
A single broad question underperforms. Split it into narrow literal Nouls and Choices, then recombine in code. A phishing bench scored 62.6% as one Jev question; five narrow signals plus a logistic regression reached 95.1% (two-line regex already hit 91.8%). The lift is the decomposition, not a better Jev prompt.
Aman Kumar · anisselbd/jev-phishing-bench · awesome-jev-usecases
04
Attention is not production
112 cataloged apps, 359 jevable listings, 7.9k stars on jev-ultrafast — almost all from days 1–4. The catalog that checked them says none were independently reproduced. Game demos outrank rigorous harnesses. Treat catalogs as usage-shape, benches as measurement.
